title: Dispatch CSA 3: Calder Survey Crosses Aperture as Returned Crew Looks On
summary: A final message reached the Institute before the receiver fell silent.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The four members of the Calder Survey crossed the eastern aperture at 6:12 this morning. Their three returned counterparts watched from an upper window. Witnesses in the yard say the older Mr. Rook struck the glass when he saw the ranging anchor carried through after the party.

The crossing was preceded by an argument. Miss Quill demanded to know why an instrument the returnees feared had been packed at all. Professor Vey answered that an unsecured aperture might close before the expedition could retrieve its measurements. Dr. Marr ordered the anchor carried but instructed the party not to set it without a direct command from the Institute.

At 6:19, the receiver transmitted an ordinary position report. At 6:41, Miss Quill described a plain of shallow water beneath an apparently stationary sky. Her next words were interrupted by a second signal in Mr. Rook’s voice: “That is the place we set it.” The younger Mr. Rook was standing beside her when the voice arrived.

The Institute cut public access to the receiving room. Our reporter heard one further sentence before the doors shut: “Do not follow the path in our bootprints.” Dr. Marr later confirmed that the signal had been recorded but declined to identify its source.

At noon, the returned Miss Bell made a request through her attendant. She asked for her workshop key, a fresh length of copper wire, and the date of tomorrow’s edition. The first two were supplied. This newspaper has agreed to provide the third.
